State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Ankush Goyal vs Samsung India on 1 March, 2016
2nd Additional Bench

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,
 PUNJAB, DAKSHIN MARG, SECTOR 37-A, CHANDIGARH.

 First Appeal No.1623 of 2014

 Date of institution: 17.12.2014
 Date of decision : 01.03.2016

 Ankush Goyal aged about 22 years son of Shri Suresh Kumar
 Goyal resident of Sekha Road, Barnala, Tehsil and District
 Barnala.

 ...Appellant/Complainant
 Versus

1. Samsung India Electronics Pvt. Ltd., B-1, Sector 81, Phase-2,
 Noida, District Gautam Budh Nagar (UP).
2. The Samsung Customer Satisfaction, 2nd Floor, Tower-C, Vipur
 Tech Square, Sector 43, Golf Course Road, Gurgaon-12202
 (Haryana).
3. Mahalaxmi Enterprises K.C. Road, Opp. Easyday, Barnala
 through its authorized signatory.
4. Samsung Care Centre/Service Centre, C/o Kamlesh Telecom,
 Opp. New Bus Stand, Barnala.
 .....Respondents/Opposite Parties

 First Appeal against the order dated
 12.09.2014 passed by the District
 Consumer Disputes Redressal
 Forum, Barnala.

 Quorum:-

 Shri Gurcharan Singh Saran, Presiding Judicial Member
 Sh. Jasbir Singh Gill, Member
 Smt. Surinder Pal Kaur, Member

 Present:-

 For the appellant :Sh. Harsh Goyal, Advocate for
 Sh.Tribhuwan Singla, Advocate
 For respondent No.1,2&4 : Sh. Sandeep Suri, Advocate
 For respondent No.3 : Service dispensed with.
 F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 2

MRS. SURINDER PAL KAUR, MEMBER

 ORDER
The appellant/complainant (hereinafter referred as

'Complainant' ) has filed the present appeal against the order dated

12.09.2014 passed by District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum,

Barnala (hereinafter referred as "District Forum") in Consumer

Complaint No.134 dated 01.07.2014 vide which complaint filed by the

complainant was dismissed being without merit.
2. Complaint was filed by the complainant under
Section 12
of the Consumer Protection Act 1986(in short `the Act') against OPs

on the averments that complainant had purchased one Samsung

Mobile GT-6312 having IMEI No.354655051167719/01 & TIN

No.03762023637 from OP No.3, after paying an amount of Rs.7,900/-

vide invoice 058. OP No.3 was dealer of OP No.1. After few days,

mobile set developed some problems and used to switch off

automatically and it's save mode also automatically became enabled

and regularly hanged. Complainant contacted OP No.4 on 24.07.2013,

regarding above said problems and OP No.4 after "minor repairs"
stated that there was some battery problem in the mobile set and due

to that mobile was not working properly. OP No.4 assured the

complainant that they had repaired the mobile set properly and that it

will function properly. After two months, mobile set again created the

same problem and complainant again contacted Op No.4 on

19.09.2013, 04.04.2014 and 10.05.2014 regarding repair of the mobile

and OP4 again and again repaired the mobile and two times the same

was repaired without opening the job cards but mobile set again

created problems and switch off automatically. On 22.05.2014, OP
F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 3
No.4 flatly refused to repair the mobile on the ground that, the warranty

period of the mobile set had expired. Complainant requested to OP

No.4 that mobile in question never worked properly from the day of its

purchase. Complainant also served a legal notice dated 23.05.2014 to

OP.4 and after receiving the notice OP4 telephonically informed the

complainant regarding repair of mobile and again OP4 repaired the

mobile set but failed to repair the mobile set properly and after that

flatly refused to repair the same. This act of OPs amounted to

deficiency in their services. Hence, he filed the complaint before the

District Forum seeking following directions against OPs:
(i) to repair the mobile set or to change the same with new

one without any labour charges;
(ii) to pay Rs.50,000/- as compensation for mental tension

 and harassment;
(iv) to pay Rs.10,000/- as litigation costs.
3. Complaint was contested by OPs. OP No.1 & 2 filed their

joint written reply by taking preliminary objections that complainant had

no cause of action against them. The handset in question was out of

warranty at the time of filing the complaint. Complaint of the

complainant did not fall under the Act as complainant had not sought

any permission to file the complaint under
section 11(2) (b)
of the Act.

These OPs had no branch office in the territorial jurisdiction of this

Hon'ble Forum as such institution of complaint by the complainant was

not maintainble. They never denied for service of mobile set even still

ready to provide the service to complainant. Complainant had filed the

present complaint with malafide intention to extract money from these

OPs and dragged into unwanted litigation. The performance of the
F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 4
mobile phone depended upon the handling of the product,

unauthorized incompatible downloading, installation of various mobile

applications, games and virus threat from internet usage also

hampered the performance of the mobile handset. Problem of hang,

switch off automatically, occurred due to software corruption.

Complainant was advised by their service engineer not to install such

applications which were not supported by the handset. However,

updated software was reloaded and the handset was made "OK"

without any charges and mobile set was delivered back to complainant

as per his satisfaction. Complainant intentionally with ulterior motive

had filed the present complaint. The liability of these OPs under terms

and conditions of warranty was to set right the product by repairing or

replacing the defective parts. No such assurance to replace the

handset was given by these OPs. However, as a goodwill gesture,

they were still ready to render the service with regard to the mobile

phone in question. Complainant had neither alleged any specific

irrepairable manufacturing defect and inferior quality of product nor

filed any documentary evidence i.e. authenticated expert report.

Complainant had sought refund or replacement of mobile set, which

was not permissible under the terms of the warranty and that

replacement or refund was permissible only where defect occurred

during the warranty period was beyond repair. On merits, they pleaded

that it was a matter of record that complainant had purchased

Samsung mobile set from OP.3 for a sum of Rs.7900 vide invoice

No.058. It was denied that after few days the mobile set created

problems and switched off automatically and save mode also

automatically enabled or regularly hanged. Complainant never

approached OP.4 on 24.07.2013 and after minor repair they stated that
F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 5
there was a battery problem in the mobile set. It was also denied that

mobile phone again and again created problem and switched off

automatically/ hanged regularly. In fact complainant himself was

negligent in handling the mobile handset in question leading to

corruption of software, resulting to hanging and auto switched off.

There was no deficiency in service. All other allegations were denied

and prayed for dismissal of the complaint with costs.
4. OP No.3 did not come present before the District Forum in

spite of due service, therefore, OP No.3 was proceeded ex-parte by

the District Forum vide order dated 22.07.2014.
5. Separate written reply was filed by OP No.4 by taking

preliminary objections that complainant had not sought permission

from the District Forum under
section 11 (2) (b)
of Act which clearly

prohibited the institution of any complaint before the District Forum if

any or all OP reside outside the territorial jurisdiction of the forum

unless and until permission was sought from the District Forum for

filling the complaint. OP had no Branch Office in the Territorial

Jurisdiction of this Forum hence the complaint was not maintainable.

The handset in question was out of warranty at the time of filing the

complaint. They never denied for service and they were still ready to

provide service to the complainant. Complainant had filed the present

complaint with malafide intention to extract money from them and

dragged this OP in unwanted litigation. The obligation of this OP under

warranty was to set right the mobile handset by repairing or replacing

the defective parts only. The performance of the mobile phone

depended upon the handling of the product, unauthorized downloading

and installation of various applications and games/virus threat from
F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 6
internet usage also hampered the performance of mobile handset. The

possibility of mishandling by the complainant or his family members

could not be ruled out. Complainant was advised not to install such

applications which were not supported by the handset. However,

updated software was reloaded and the handset was made OK without

any charges and handset was delivered back to complainant to his

satisfaction. It was denied that any assurance to replace the hand set

was given to complainant under the terms of warranty and that as

goodwill gesture this OP was still ready to render services with regard

to mobile phone in question, if required. On merits, it was pleaded that

it was a matter of record that complainant had purchased Samsung

mobile from OP No.3 for Rs.7900/- vide invoice No.058. It was denied

that after few days the mobile created problem and switched off

automatically save mode also automatically enabled or regularly

hanged. There was no battery problem and no assurance was given to

the complainant that mobile will not create problem in future. It was

denied that after two months there was same problem or that

complainant contacted this OP on 19.09.2013, 04.04.2014 and

10.05.2014 repeatedly. They never refused to repair the handset.

There was no deficiency in their service rather whenever complainant

had submitted his handset with this OP the same was serviced,

problem was rectified without any charges and handset was delivered

back in OK condition. Complainant was not entitled for replacement of

mobile and refund of price. Under warranty this OP was only liable to

repair or replace the defective parts. There was no deficiency in their

service and prayed for dismissal of the complaint with costs.
6. The parties were allowed by the learned District Forum to

lead their evidence.
F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 7
7. In support of the averments, the complainant had tendered

into evidence his affidavit Ex C-1 along with other documents Ex.C-1 to

Ex.C-10 and closed their evidence. On other hand OPs had tendered

into evidence affidavit of Sh. Shriniwas Joshi, Senior Manager

Samsung India Electronics Pvt. Ltd. Ludhiana as Ex.OP-1,2 & 4/1

along with other documents Ex.OP-1,2 & 4 to Ex.OP-1,2 & 4/3 and

closed their evidence.
8. After going through the allegations alleged in the

complaint, written reply filed by OPs evidence and documents brought

on the record, the learned District Forum dismissed the complaint as

referred above.
9. Aggrieved against the order passed by District forum

appellant/ complainant has preferred the present complaint.
10. We have heard learned counsel for both the parties and

carefully gone through the record of the District Forum.
11. It was submitted by the learned counsel for the

complainant that District Forum without appreciating the entire

evidence dismissed the complaint on the ground that there was no

merit in the complaint whereas, complainant approached to OPs many

times personally and telephonically requested to repair the mobile

phone or to change the same with new one. Mobile set continuously

created problems and switch off automatically. Its save mode also

automatically enabled and regularly hanged. On 24.07.2013,

complainant contacted OP No.4 regarding the above said problem and

this OP after minor repairs of the same stated that there was some

battery problem and due to that mobile was not functioning properly

and also assured that said mobile will not again create any problem,
F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 8
but after few days there was same problem in the mobile set and he

again contacted to OP No.4 on 19.09.2013, 04.04.2014, 10.05.2014

and OP NO.4 again and again repaired the mobile set and two times

the same was repaired without opening the job card. On 22.05.2014,

complainant contacted OP No.4 but he flatly refused to repair the

same, saying that there was no warranty period on the said mobile

whereas complainant made a request to OP No.4 that mobile in

question never worked properly from the day of its purchase and he

faced the problems regularly. Whereas, the District Forum observed

that complainant had failed to prove any manufacturing defect in the

mobile set and also mentioned that complainant failed to bring any

evidence on record that auto switch off mobile was not the result of

corruption of its software. Whereas, the job card itself speak and prove

the allegations of the complainant. He prayed for to set-aside the

impugned order and acceptance of the appeal.
12. On the other hand, counsel for the OPs has submitted that

District Forum had returned the correct findings that complainant had

failed to prove any manufacturing defect and onus was on the

complainant to bring an expert report to prove that hanging and auto

switch of mobile was not the result of corruption of its software. They

prayed for the dismissal of the appeal and to upheld the impugned

order.
13. Complainant had purchased the Samsung mobile Model

No.6312 with the warranty of one year vide invoice 058 dated

10.05.2013 for a sum of Rs.7900/- from OP No.3 (Ex.C-1). It was

specific allegation of the complainant that after few days of its

purchase the mobile handset created some problem and switch off
F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 9
automatically, its save mode also automatically enabled and regularly

hanged. He has placed on record a job card dated 24.07.2013 (Ex.C-2)

in which defect description mentioned as "HANG PROBLEM AND

AUTO SWITCH OFF". He further proved job card dated 19.09.2013

Ex.C-4 where problem was mentioned as poor battery and auto-switch.

Complainant vide job card dated 04.04.2014 (Ex.C-5) draw our

attention where problem was mentioned as hang problem and auto-

switch off, sometime red line show on display. Further, as per job

card dated 10.05.2014 (Ex.C-6) the problem was Auto Switch off and

save mode auto enabled, sometime network problem.
14. From perusal of these job cards it is clearly revealed that

complainant approached OPs again and again with same problem i.e.

hang problem and auto switch off. The first job card dated 24.07.2013

is just after two months from the date of purchase i.e. 10.05.2013. OPs

took the plea that the performance of mobile phone depended upon the

handling of the product. According to them the alleged problem of

hang, switch off automatically occurred due to software corruption,

installation of non-compatible mobile application and games and also

pleaded that there was no expert report that the mobile set was

hanged due to manufacturing defect. No doubt, with the expert report

Forum can easily determine who is at fault. However, from the job card

it is very much clear that the mobile set created again and again the

same problem i.e. HANG PROBLEM AND AUTO SWITCH OFF".

When the problem was clearly mentioned in the job cards then there

was need of any expert report. The "Defect Description" mentioned in

the job cards dated 24.07.2013 to 10.05.2014 (Ex.C-2 to Ex.C-5) was

not denied by OPs. There was no evidence on the record that OPs had

warned the complainant regarding downloading unauthorized
F.A. No. 1623 of 2014 10
applications. Under the warranty period OPs were liable to repair or

replace the defective parts of the product. Complainant has purchased

the same with the assurance that it will work smoothly and within a

short span of time he had to go to the service centre of OPs number of

time. Therefore, OPs are under legal obligation to redress the

grievances of the complainant. Whereas District Forum did not give

proper appreciation on the job cards. It is not necessary that only in

case of manufacturing defect they will replace the defective parts. It is

their obligation to check why same type of problem is occurring in the

set. They are required to rectify the problem in the set during warranty

period.
15. In view of the above discussion the appeal of the
complainant is allowed. The order of the District Forum is set aside.
OPs are directed to repair the handset within 2 weeks from the day of
hand over the same. If the mobile set is not in repairable condition then
OPs are jointly and severally liable to refund the price of the mobile set
within 45 days from the receipt of the copy of this order. It was further
directed to pay Rs. 5000/- as compensation for mental tension and
harassment and litigation costs.
16. The arguments in this appeal were heard on 05.02.2016
and the order was reserved. Now, the order be communicated to the
parties as per rules.
17. The appeal could not be decided within the statutory
period due to heavy pendency of court cases.
(GURCHARAN SINGH SARAN)
 PRESIDING JUDICIAL MEMBER

 (JASBIR SINGH GILL)
 MEMBER

 (SURINDER PAL KAUR)
